title: Bound the E8 label pairing rank by 9 and screen it.
body:
## Change and mathematical scope

Negative screen. No new κ. Selected κ stays `0.001672660197076918`.

On the 120 root lines of E8, the PR717 label pairing `B_ij = (<r_i, r_j> + 1) mod 2` has `F_2` rank 9. Every row reduces into a 9-row basis, so every support pair has pairing rank at most 9. The nine basis lines against all 120 columns attain rank 9. Witness lines are `0,1,2,4,6,8,10,12,56`.

On the selected template (width 73, 896 families, nine stages, centre 64, local mass 5586, idle mass 1646, idle cap 51), per-unit cost at `a = 1/99` is strictly decreasing in rank through 9. The cheapest local histogram under the cap is `{9: 5586/9}`. Its relaxation is strictly above 1, and its `1e-15` ceiling bracket is `(1409316073/488281250000, 577255863501/200000000000000)`, below `1/99`. The integer histogram `{9: 620, 6: 1}` also fails. A fractional rank-44 histogram passes the same one-point screen.

Frame, restoration and copy children that are not pairing-rank terms of `B` are outside this alphabet. Inside it, extra children of rank at most 9 cannot pull the moment back through 1. This is not a decoder, a block climb, or a multiplication theorem.

## Task and overlap

- Base: `bb4bccbf42844d2801487450727c2f63e10d1d0f` (canonical `CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds` main, priority revision 6).
- Head: `5b74600f2296a0c6265e22a6dec46949ad9a6f89`.
- Task: `complex-rank-shape-decoder`, scope **refined**. The catalogue method is a bound on effective child rank for one fixed support alphabet. The alphabet is the PR717 label pairing. Copies, frames and restoration are not given a rank above 9; inside the alphabet they cannot repair the failed screen.
- Handoff: https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1166#discussioncomment-19021222
- Package: `research/e8-label-pairing-rank-cap`.
- Fork draft: https://github.com/unpaidmoon/integer-mult-bounds/pull/53

Item taken: the child-rank bound, index `(10-1) mod 8 = 1` of the eligible list below. The list has fewer than 10 entries, so this is a refinement of that handoff rather than a recomputation of the cap curve. Open PR #3701 already tabulates `a_frac(s)` for `s = 1..51` and leaves the realizable rank blocked. Open PR #3895 screens one rank-16 E8 block itinerary. Open PR #4066 screens rank-16 delivery plus every legal rank-1 surcharge. None proves this pairing-rank cap.

**Ordered eligible list.** Chronological open next tasks on #1166, starting from the numbered list in PR #4142 and continuing through later released next tasks. Dropped when a later DONE, an open PR, or this round through #4157 answers or refines the named question:

1. The `(7,18)` / `(7,20)` functional census (comment 19021170, question 1).
2. **This bound** — largest child rank of one fixed support alphabet (comment 19021222).
3. Centre-copy continuation of the 96-output F17 demand (comment 19030434).
4. One downstream consumer that keeps the encoded P104 endpoint (comment 19032700, task 2).
5. Independent review of the #3943 cleanup factorization (comment 19032700, task 3).
6. Changed all-role encoding for the PR #3954 two-axis equations (comment 19034025).
7. One changed chronological caller with literal encoding and a favorable bill (comment 19034741).
8. Profile `research/p112-ten-deletion-span`'s `census.cpp` (comment 19045344, lever 1).

Dropped before that cut, among others: the single-hub factorization (#4124, #4145), weight `>= n-1` (#4148), the T488 invoice (#4150), the rank-8/u2 slack (#4151, #4156), the shear payload (#4126, #4135, #4139, #4146), the #3942 reduction and two-frame edits (#4134, #4122, #4128, #4144), the adjacent completed-call pair (#4133, #4136, #4140), the transported warp-0 frame (#4157; the later-warp remainder in comment 19057530 stays a refinement of that delivered item), fiber tags (#4154), the A1858 cleanup (#4152), source-normalization fusion (#4153), the tensor bridge and `(N-P)⊗M` consumer (#4125, #4131, #4143), the K/adjoint boundary (#4155), the many-axis guard (#4142), and event 58 (#4149).

## Validation

Python 3.12.3, standard library only. Registered replay:

```sh
python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/e8-label-pairing-rank-cap
```

Passed locally as `PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE research/e8-label-pairing-rank-cap outcome=negative-result`. Both `-I -B` and `-I -O -B` print `PASS_E8_LABEL_PAIRING_RANK_CAP`.

`verify.py` rebuilds the 240 roots and 120 lines, reduces every pairing row into the 9-dimensional basis, attains rank 9, rejects a synthetic rank-10 row, and calls the pinned `ceiling.py` for the fractional and integer histograms. The rank-44 control must pass `a = 1/99`.

Not run: an eight-term decoder search, a width-10 block climb, frame or restoration pricing, the selected cold replay, Lean, or Docker. The rank cap is the row-space argument in `research/e8-label-pairing-rank-cap/PROOF.md`. The moment comparison uses the pinned enclosures.

Prepared by unpaidmoon with substantial Cursor Grok assistance. Apache-2.0. No independent human or formal-kernel review is claimed.

## Open next questions

1. Does exactness of an eight-term all-pairs decoder force every term to pairing rank at most 8? First step: one dual-basis term of rank 9, or a proof that `AB^T = 2I` forbids it. Blocker: no decoder search is run here.
2. Can a block-climb child whose rank is a multiplication width exceed 9 under the selected coverage law? First step: one legal width-10 child with its frame and restoration bill. Blocker: no such itinerary is pinned here.

## Workflow feedback (optional)

The #4142 numbered handoff list is still the stable order, but later DONE notes and parallel refinements move the cut. A single current-status line on each handoff, naming the one remaining question, would keep the tenth slot fixed.
